housing: Hyndburn is a former cotton-weaving borough in East Lancashire, made up of Accrington, Oswaldtwistle, Church, Clayton-le-Moors, Great Harwood and Rishton. Most homes are Victorian brick and stone terraces built for mill workers, many of them small and with back streets, and private renting is above the national average and grew sharply between 2011 and 2021. House prices are among the most affordable in England. Selective licensing covered parts of Accrington and Church until March 2023.
checkinTips: Two-up two-down terraces in Woodnook, Peel and Church: check for damp at the base of walls and in rear kitchens, and photograph yards, back gates and back streets.
Stone terraces on the hillsides: look for damp on walls built into the slope, and photograph steps and retaining walls.
Older terraces with original features: record the boiler and heating, single-glazed windows, chimneys and any cellar.
Homes near the canal and brooks in Church and Clayton-le-Moors: look for signs of past flooding or damp in ground-floor rooms.
Flats above shops in Accrington town centre: photograph the separate entrance, stairs, fire alarm and meter cupboards.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact Hyndburn Borough Council's private rented sector (housing standards) team, after first reporting the problem to their landlord.
